findings.issue: ADR §4 RED-LINES explicitly lists 'lossy live-migration' as a categorical human-gate operation (alongside drop/rename/lossy type-change). The spec operation table and AuthoringOpKind vocabulary omit this operation entirely, and Out of Scope (spec §5) does not account for it. This leaves a gap between the ADR red-lines coverage claim and the actual implementation scope.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) add 'live_migration' to AuthoringOpKind with classification destructive/core_pinned and AC-19 test, or (b) add to spec §5 Out of Scope: 'Lossy live-migration (Camunda-grade instance rerouting) — covered by separate task (TODO: assign task number)'.

findings.issue: Spec §1 Confirm-contract explicitly promises three validation checks, including '2. Подтверждение не является одним из запрещённых шаблонов (автозаполнение).' isValidConfirm in src/core/authoring-redlines.ts:265-273 implements only rule 1 (length >= 10) and rule 3 (force === true). Rule 2 (forbidden template check) is absent from implementation and has no corresponding AC or test. Spec-impl mismatch on stated validation contract.
findings.suggestion: Option A (minimal): remove rule 2 from spec §1 and add a comment in isValidConfirm acknowledging that semantic validation is delegated to the UI layer (T-0073). Option B (full): implement FORBIDDEN_STATEMENTS list, enforce in isValidConfirm, add AC-19 test.

findings.issue: Spec summary table labels core/system-directory-field operations as 'destructive (всегда, без core-check)' but the actual AuthoringChangeClass value is 'core_pinned' (a distinct third classification). FR-2 and ACs AC-8/AC-9 correctly use 'core_pinned'. Summary table is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Change table cell to 'core_pinned (безусловный deny, escape-hatch запрещён §5)'.
